title: WPSS/1571/2020 of AJAY SINGH THAKUR Vs UNION OF INDIA

paras.text:
WPSS No. 1571 of 2020
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
ia Video Conferencing) (v

Mr. Nalin Saun, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Azmeen, Standing Counsel for Union of
India/ respondent no. 1.
Mr. Siddharath Sah, learned counsel for the
respondent Bank.
The petitioner, in the present writ petition, has
challenged the impugned order dated 30.09.2020, as
has been passed by the respondent no. 4, whereby
petitioner's services have been transferred from
ROSARB, Dehradun, Regional Office to Chandigarh
Zone.
The facts, which are reflected from the writ
petition, are that the petitioner, apparently being
aggrieved by the order of transfer, has preferred a
representation, before the competent authority and as
per order dated 01.10.2020 which was passed by the
Regional Head (AGM), who has been arrayed as
private respondent no. 4, had rejected the
representation. As a consequence thereto, petitioner has
been relieved from the place, in order to enable him to
join at the transferred place. Order of rejection of
representation, has not been put to challenge, in the
present writ petition. Apart from it, the order itself
shows that petitioner services have been relieved on
03.10.2020, in order to enable him, to join at the
transferred place.
Learned counsel for the petitioner argues that
there are certain terms and conditions, which have been
laid down in the policy, as enforced by the Bank of
Baroda; for the purposes of regulating transfers of the
employees of the Bank and in accordance with the
Clause 3 of the Policy, the petitioner's services ought
not to have been transferred, within a period of three
years from the date of his previous transfer.
This Court has asked a question, to the counsel
for the petitioner, as to what is the statutory effect of

this Policy of the Bank whether it could be enforced
under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. No
plausible explanation has been given by the learned
counsel for the petitioner, except that where will the
petitioner go?
In case, there is no forum available to the
petitioner where the petitioner could go for redressal of
his grievance, this itself will not provide enforceability
of the Policy of the Bank, which is only an
administrative policy, by invoking the writ jurisdiction,
under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. Apart
from it, transfer is an administrative exigency of
service and transfer order has been passed in exercise
of administrative powers, therefore, this Court finds no
merit in the writ petition. Accordingly, the writ petition
is dismissed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 05.12.2020
SKS
